principles.title: Typed versioned APIs
principles.statement: Parse every API request into a typed, versioned contract and return only structured safe responses and errors.
principles.rationale: Trust-boundary validation and deliberate versions let clients and services evolve without admitting ambiguous data.
principles.evidence: Contract tests cover accepted, rejected, unknown, and prior-version payloads; breaking changes use a declared version; errors omit secrets, stack traces, and internal identifiers.

principles.title: Persistence-aware services
principles.statement: Access persistence through an owned data contract and deploy schema-dependent service behavior only after a forward-safe migration path exists.
principles.rationale: Service correctness depends on storage ownership and schema compatibility even when persistence is implemented behind another module.
principles.evidence: Service code names its store owner and data contract; access is typed and parameterized; deployment tests prove old and new service versions tolerate the migration sequence.

principles.title: Server-enforced authorization
principles.statement: Source secrets outside code and enforce authentication and authorization server-side with default-deny decisions.
principles.rationale: Client checks and missing configuration cannot protect server resources or machine-triggered operations.
principles.evidence: Authorization tests cover absent, invalid, and insufficient credentials; denied requests perform no protected action; no secret is committed or returned.

principles.title: Retry-safe service degradation
principles.statement: Make retryable writes idempotent and bound every service dependency with explicit timeout, backoff, rate, and degraded-result behavior.
principles.rationale: Partial failure and retries are normal distributed-system conditions and must not duplicate effects or masquerade as success.
principles.evidence: Repeated write fixtures produce one effect; dependency tests exercise timeout, rate limit, and unavailable states; telemetry distinguishes success, degradation, and failure.

principles.title: Minimal directed boundaries
principles.statement: Choose the smallest explicit boundary that keeps dependencies acyclic and each fact in one authoritative home.
principles.rationale: Narrow, directional seams limit coordination and prevent implementation details from becoming accidental contracts.
principles.evidence: Dependency graphs contain no cycles; boundary records name assets, entry points, trust assumptions, and owners; duplicate sources of truth are absent.

principles.title: Explicit additive contracts
principles.statement: Publish typed, versioned, consumer-neutral contracts and evolve them additively until a declared breaking boundary.
principles.rationale: Stable contracts let implementations and platforms change independently without surprising consumers.
principles.evidence: Compatibility tests exercise old and new consumers; schemas classify additive and breaking changes; policy modules run without a renderer or consumer framework.

principles.title: Durable decisions
principles.statement: Record consequential architectural tradeoffs as ADRs before treating them as durable constraints.
principles.rationale: Future maintainers need the forces and consequences behind a decision, not only its surviving implementation.
principles.evidence: Each consequential durable choice links to a Proposed or Accepted ADR; routine implementation choices do not create records.

principles.title: Reproducible construction
principles.statement: Require equivalent declared inputs to produce equivalent build outputs.
principles.rationale: Reproducibility is an architectural property needed for trustworthy diagnosis, release, and recovery.
principles.evidence: Clean repeated builds match by digest or a documented normalized comparison; undeclared environment state does not alter outputs.

principles.title: Declared deterministic build graph
principles.statement: Build only through a declared acyclic dependency graph whose equivalent inputs produce equivalent outputs.
principles.rationale: Hidden ordering and undeclared state make failures irreproducible and artifacts untraceable.
principles.evidence: Graph validation finds no cycles or undeclared edges; generated output is regenerated and matches source; clean repeated builds match by digest or documented normalization; parallel scheduling preserves results.

principles.title: Immutable versioned artifacts
principles.statement: Produce immutable versioned artifacts and never mutate or rebuild an already identified release.
principles.rationale: A release identifier is trustworthy only when it always resolves to the same bytes and provenance.
principles.evidence: Registries reject replacement; repeated retrieval matches the recorded digest; corrections create a new version and artifact.

principles.title: Additive semantic evolution
principles.statement: Version public contracts with SemVer intent at authoring time and evolve them additively until a declared migration permits a breaking release.
principles.rationale: Consumers need compatibility expectations before a change reaches packaging or release.
principles.evidence: Change records classify patch, minor, and major intent; compatibility tests exercise supported versions; breaking changes include migration and deprecation evidence.

principles.title: Generated changesets and changelogs
principles.statement: Record release intent in reviewed changesets and generate versions and changelogs from those records instead of editing release output by hand.
principles.rationale: Author-time intent is more accurate and auditable than reconstructing user-visible changes at publish time.
principles.evidence: Releasable changes include a reviewed change record; generation is deterministic; each changelog entry resolves to its change and pull request.

principles.title: Clean reproducible environments
principles.statement: Run authoritative build and release checks in clean environments with pinned toolchains, frozen dependencies, and no production credentials.
principles.rationale: Residual files, floating tools, and live secrets make release evidence irreproducible and unsafe.
principles.evidence: Authoritative checks emit required evidence for every pull request and release candidate; a clean install and build succeed from declared inputs; tool and dependency versions are recorded; fixtures replace production credentials.

principles.title: Build dependency hygiene
principles.statement: Keep build dependencies minimal, locked, reviewed, and free of unnecessary install-time execution.
principles.rationale: Every build dependency expands compromise, nondeterminism, maintenance, and licensing surface.
principles.evidence: Dependency review records purpose and provenance; frozen installation succeeds with lifecycle scripts disabled unless justified; stale or duplicate tools are removed.

principles.title: Release artifact identity
principles.statement: Bind every release artifact to its version, commit revision, source change records, checks, and runtime-reported identity.
principles.rationale: Operators cannot verify or diagnose a deployment when the running bytes cannot be traced to reviewed source and evidence.
principles.evidence: Provenance resolves artifact digest to version, commit, changesets, pull requests, and required checks; runtime identity matches the deployed artifact.

principles.title: Rollback-compatible releases
principles.statement: Preserve rollback compatibility across code, contract, schema, and artifact activation boundaries for the declared recovery window.
principles.rationale: Rollback is unsafe when a newer release irreversibly changes state or consumers before recovery can complete.
principles.evidence: Release tests exercise old and new versions through migration and rollback order; activation is atomic; recovery instructions name compatibility limits and artifact identity.

principles.title: Owned durable integrity
principles.statement: Give every durable store and schema one owner, enforce invariants in the data model, and migrate through reviewed forward-safe steps.
principles.rationale: Durable data outlives individual service versions and needs explicit integrity and recovery boundaries.
principles.evidence: Ownership is recorded; typed parameterized access, constraints, and required indexes are tested; migrations are reviewed, observable, recoverable, and compatible with their deployment sequence.

principles.title: Versioned bounded data contracts
principles.statement: Version event and interchange schemas, bound their names and cardinality, and reject unrecognized shapes.
principles.rationale: Governed schemas keep analytical and operational consumers stable while preventing accidental high-cardinality data growth.
principles.evidence: Schema validation runs before release; compatibility fixtures cover supported versions; taxonomy and cardinality checks reject unknown or unbounded fields.

principles.title: Minimized governed data
principles.statement: Minimize data at collection and implement consent, retention, export, erasure, anonymization, and audit mechanisms only from an explicit authorized obligation.
principles.rationale: Privacy-preserving mechanics reduce exposure without letting Engineering invent the policy or legal basis for processing.
principles.evidence: Payload reviews prefer scoped identifiers, enums, aggregates, and buckets; cross-product identity is not reversible; lifecycle tests verify the referenced Product-owned obligation.

principles.title: Thin typed adapters
principles.statement: Parse external input into a typed, versioned contract and isolate provider or framework behavior behind thin single-purpose adapters.
principles.rationale: External systems change independently, so their assumptions must stop at a narrow replaceable seam.
principles.evidence: Contract tests cover invalid and prior-version input; middleware ordering is explicit; internal modules do not expose vendor types; adapter replacement tests preserve the contract.

principles.title: Explicit seam caches
principles.statement: Make every integration cache explicit, keyed, bounded, and invalidatable without allowing it to become the source of truth.
principles.rationale: Hidden or unbounded cache behavior turns temporary optimization into stale authority.
principles.evidence: Cache tests cover key isolation, expiry, invalidation, misses, and upstream recovery; bypassing the cache preserves correctness.

principles.title: Typed retry-safe failures
principles.statement: Propagate typed safe integration errors and make retryable seam operations idempotent with explicit degraded and failed results.
principles.rationale: Boundary failures must remain actionable without leaking internals, duplicating effects, or returning success-shaped fallbacks.
principles.evidence: Error mapping is exhaustive; logs and responses omit sensitive data; repeated-operation fixtures produce one effect; degradation tests distinguish success from failure.

principles.title: Observable seams
principles.statement: Observe integration latency, outcome, cache behavior, and upstream health without recording secrets or sensitive payloads.
principles.rationale: A seam cannot be operated or degraded deliberately when its behavior is indistinguishable from internal work.
principles.evidence: Boundary telemetry identifies the integration and typed outcome; dashboards or traces expose latency and upstream health; payload review finds no secret or sensitive body capture.

principles.title: Credential proxy isolation
principles.statement: Keep third-party credentials server-side behind a narrow proxy with explicit origin and operation allowlists and no user-data persistence.
principles.rationale: A constrained proxy enables browser integration without exposing credentials or becoming an undeclared backend.
principles.evidence: Clients contain no provider secret; proxy tests reject unlisted origins and operations; storage inspection confirms no user-data persistence; credentials are sourced outside code.

principles.title: Local durable ownership
principles.statement: Treat the device's durable store as the system of record, persist before reflecting success, and keep portable data exportable.
principles.rationale: Local-first behavior is a trust contract only when core work and user-owned data survive network and account loss.
principles.evidence: Offline tests complete core writes and full portable-data export; durable-write failures are surfaced; portable and device-local data are distinct in types and storage.

principles.title: Optional sync seam
principles.statement: Put product-data sync behind one narrow provider contract without making core local operation wait for an account, provider, or network.
principles.rationale: Sync is an optional replication layer, not the authority for local-first data.
principles.evidence: Core reads and writes pass with the provider absent; provider contract tests cover upload, download, retry, and unavailable states; local data remains authoritative.

principles.title: Declared conflict model
principles.statement: Declare and test ordering, tombstone, concurrency, and merge rules for every synchronized data type.
principles.rationale: Implicit conflict behavior loses data unpredictably and cannot be reasoned about during offline edits.
principles.evidence: Conflict fixtures cover concurrent create, update, delete, replay, and clock-order cases; merge results satisfy documented invariants.

principles.title: Zero-config safe degradation
principles.statement: Start core local operation with zero external-service configuration and degrade unavailable optional services to explicit local behavior.
principles.rationale: Optional dependencies must not block local ownership or turn an unavailable service into data loss or false success.
principles.evidence: Zero-config tests complete core flows; unavailable-service tests preserve writes, avoid false success, and require no account or provider handshake.

principles.title: Structured operational signals
principles.statement: Emit structured, bounded operational signals that identify the component, operation, outcome, duration, and deployment version.
principles.rationale: Operators cannot compare or route unstructured events reliably across versions and components.
principles.evidence: Signal schemas constrain names, types, and cardinality; representative operations emit success, degradation, and failure outcomes with version identity.

principles.title: Live service identity
principles.statement: Expose a cheap, time-bounded, uncached health signal that reports service state and deployed version without sensitive detail.
principles.rationale: Availability evidence must identify what is running without turning a health endpoint into a costly dependency or disclosure surface.
principles.evidence: External probes receive bounded responses with version and build revision; responses use no-store semantics and expose only coarse state.

principles.title: Bounded dependency checks
principles.statement: Bound dependency checks with operation-specific timeouts, retry and rate limits, and explicit unconfigured, degraded, and unavailable results.
principles.rationale: Unbounded checks and retries can turn one dependency failure into exhaustion or a retry storm.
principles.evidence: Tests exercise absent configuration, timeout, rate limit, backoff, and recovery; health remains bounded and distinguishes intentional absence from failure.

principles.title: End-to-end correlation
principles.statement: Correlate work across trust and dependency boundaries with propagated identifiers that are unique, bounded, and unrelated to sensitive identity.
principles.rationale: A failure spanning components cannot be reconstructed when each signal describes an isolated operation.
principles.evidence: Traces and logs connect ingress, internal work, and egress; missing or malformed identifiers are replaced safely; identifiers reveal no user or payload data.

principles.title: Redacted observable evidence
principles.statement: Redact secrets and sensitive payloads before telemetry leaves the producing boundary, and retain only the minimum evidence needed to diagnose behavior.
principles.rationale: Central observability multiplies exposure when producers emit raw credentials, content, or regulated data.
principles.evidence: Schema allowlists and adversarial fixtures reject sensitive fields; retention follows a referenced obligation; audit signals record actor, action, target, and time without payload.

principles.title: SLO evidence
principles.statement: Define each service-level indicator with an objective, window, measurement source, and alert condition, then retain evidence for release and incident review.
principles.rationale: Operational reliability cannot be evaluated from health checks or business metrics without a stable user-impact measure and objective.
principles.evidence: Each SLI and SLO has a versioned definition, query or calculation, owner, alert, and retained evaluation history; business metrics remain separately owned.

principles.title: Predictable degradation
principles.statement: Define and observe degraded behavior so authentication and mutations fail closed while only explicitly safe non-critical reads may fail soft.
principles.rationale: Partial failure must not silently expand authority, lose writes, or masquerade as complete success.
principles.evidence: Failure-mode tests classify each operation; telemetry distinguishes healthy, degraded, and failed results; recovery avoids duplicate effects and retry storms.

principles.title: Reproducible measurements
principles.statement: Measure every performance claim with a reproducible command, controlled environment, declared cold or warm state, baseline, and before-and-after delta.
principles.rationale: Uncontrolled observations cannot distinguish an implementation effect from cache, hardware, network, or workload variance.
principles.evidence: Results record command, revision, platform, workload, state, repetitions, summary statistic, baseline, and delta.

principles.title: Versioned performance budgets
principles.statement: Define versioned, owned, method-specific performance budgets and review them when architecture or target platforms materially change.
principles.rationale: A threshold without scope, ownership, and measurement method cannot govern regressions consistently.
principles.evidence: Each budget names metric, workload, platform, method, threshold, owner, version, and review trigger; deterministic signals block while unstable lab signals remain advisory.

principles.title: Minimal package surface
principles.statement: Budget package, export, and dependency cost while preserving minimal tree-shakeable entry points.
principles.rationale: Consumers should not pay delivery or initialization cost for unrelated capabilities.
principles.evidence: Package and route analyses attribute bytes and dependencies to entry points; unused exports are removable; regressions identify the introducing change.

principles.title: Correctness-preserving caches
principles.statement: Use content-addressed bounded caches only to accelerate deterministic work, and preserve correctness and diagnosability on miss, staleness, or bypass.
principles.rationale: A cache is an optimization, not an authority or substitute for verification.
principles.evidence: Keys include all declared inputs; hit, miss, stale, invalidation, and bypass tests produce correct results; telemetry distinguishes cache outcomes.

principles.title: Foreground responsiveness
principles.statement: Prefer foreground responsiveness over background throughput and make background work yield under active demand.
principles.rationale: Aggregate throughput is not useful when current interaction becomes blocked or unpredictable.
principles.evidence: Concurrent-load tests bound foreground latency; schedulers yield or prioritize foreground work; background throughput remains observable.

principles.title: Bounded fallible work
principles.statement: Bound long or fallible operations with explicit progress, timeout, cancellation or failure, and a signal that distinguishes progressing from stuck.
principles.rationale: Unbounded work consumes resources and leaves callers unable to decide whether to wait, retry, or recover.
principles.evidence: Timeout and cancellation tests terminate work; progress advances monotonically or reports an explicit indeterminate state; stuck detection is exercised.

principles.title: Platform-native profiling
principles.statement: Profile suspected bottlenecks with the platform-native tool and record a recipe that another engineer can reproduce.
principles.rationale: Optimization without attributed runtime evidence often moves cost or treats a symptom rather than its cause.
principles.evidence: Profiles retain workload, tool, platform, revision, capture settings, and attributed hot path; the same recipe confirms the change.

principles.title: Quantified regression triage
principles.statement: Reproduce, quantify, bisect, and route every material performance regression to the owning boundary before changing its budget.
principles.rationale: Moving a threshold hides regressions when the cause and accountable component remain unknown.
principles.evidence: Triage records baseline, magnitude, first bad revision or bounded range, owner, disposition, and confirming measurement.

principles.title: Assurance precedence
principles.statement: Reject performance changes that weaken correctness, accessibility, privacy, or security.
principles.rationale: Faster incorrect or exclusionary behavior is a regression, not an optimization.
principles.evidence: Optimization reviews assess each precedence property; tests show preserved behavior; exceptions are not accepted as performance tradeoffs.

principles.title: Secret lifecycle
principles.statement: Keep secrets out of source, artifacts, logs, and clients; inject them at runtime, detect exposure independently, and rotate every exposed value.
principles.rationale: Deleting a leaked value does not revoke copies or protect environments that accepted it.
principles.evidence: Repository, artifact, client, and log scans find no secret; runtime injection is documented; exposure drills revoke and replace the value.

principles.title: Verified supply chain
principles.statement: Verify a minimal locked dependency chain, suppress unneeded install execution, pin external build actions immutably, and resolve exploitable or prohibited inputs before release.
principles.rationale: Build dependencies and automation execute with the product's trust even when application code does not call them directly.
principles.evidence: Frozen lockfile installation succeeds; dependency review records necessity, provenance, vulnerabilities, licenses, and lifecycle scripts; exploitable HIGH or CRITICAL findings block release until remediation or Product-owned risk acceptance; external actions use immutable revisions.

principles.title: Boundary threat models
principles.statement: Record assets, entry points, trust boundaries, abuse paths, and mitigations before introducing or materially changing a security boundary.
principles.rationale: Security controls cannot be reviewed coherently when the protected assets and attacker paths remain implicit.
principles.evidence: Boundary changes link a reviewed threat model; named mitigations map to tests or operational evidence; unresolved risks name an owner.

principles.title: Least authority
principles.statement: Enforce default-deny authentication and authorization with the least privilege, scope, and credential lifetime needed for each operation.
principles.rationale: Broad or implicit authority turns one compromised identity or component into unrelated access.
principles.evidence: Authorization tests cover absent, invalid, cross-tenant, cross-role, and cross-resource access; credentials and file permissions are scoped and time-bounded.

principles.title: Trust-boundary validation
principles.statement: Parse, schema-check, and bound every trust-boundary input, then parameterize or encode it for the exact storage, execution, path, or output context.
principles.rationale: Untrusted data becomes dangerous when its shape, size, path, or interpretation reaches a more privileged sink.
principles.evidence: Negative tests reject malformed, oversized, traversal, injection, and unsupported input; paths remain under declared roots; output tests verify context-appropriate encoding.

principles.title: Risk-focused security review
principles.statement: Run an OWASP-aligned security review when authentication, input, dependency, or build boundaries change, and track each finding through remediation or explicit risk acceptance.
principles.rationale: Passing automated checks does not prove that design-level abuse paths or contextual vulnerabilities were considered.
principles.evidence: Triggering changes link a review; findings record category, severity, exploitability, impact, owner, disposition, and regression evidence.

principles.title: Secure failure
principles.statement: Fail closed at security decisions, reject unsafe configuration before service, and map faults once to stable errors that disclose no sensitive internals.
principles.rationale: Ambiguous startup and success-shaped fallbacks can bypass controls while verbose failures leak exploitable context.
principles.evidence: Boot and request tests reject missing critical configuration; denied operations produce no protected effect; responses, logs, caches, and artifacts omit stacks, queries, internal IDs, and secrets.

principles.title: Privacy-minimizing lifecycle evidence
principles.statement: Minimize personal data and produce auditable lifecycle evidence for each authorized collection, use, retention, export, correction, deletion, consent, and processor control.
principles.rationale: Privacy mechanisms are trustworthy only when they implement an explicit obligation and prove effects across derived stores without exposing payloads.
principles.evidence: An obligation-linked inventory names source, category, purpose, owner, control, retention, residency, processor, and evidence; rights and consent tests use synthetic data; audit records contain actor, action, target, and time but no payload.

principles.title: Layered test portfolio
principles.statement: Build a test pyramid with many isolated domain tests, fewer real-seam integration and contract tests, and thin end-to-end coverage of critical paths.
principles.rationale: Fast direct feedback and selective seam realism find different failures without making every check depend on the whole system.
principles.evidence: Domain rules run without framework or network setup; integration tests cross real owned seams; end-to-end tests are limited to named critical outcomes.

principles.title: Contract-focused assertions
principles.statement: Test stable public behavior and producer-consumer contracts instead of incidental implementation structure.
principles.rationale: Refactoring should not break assurance when externally observable behavior remains correct.
principles.evidence: Assertions exercise public inputs, outputs, errors, schemas, compatibility, migrations, and distributed artifacts without reaching private internals.

principles.title: Regression boundaries
principles.statement: Add a failing regression test at the narrowest authoritative boundary for every new behavior, corrected defect, or changed shared contract.
principles.rationale: A fix without evidence at the decision boundary can regress through another caller or implementation path.
principles.evidence: The test fails before the fix, passes after it, names the defect cause, and exercises the layer where the rule is obeyed.

principles.title: Distinct static signals
principles.statement: Separate type, lint, build, format, and security checks from behavior tests, and make statically decidable invariants blocking at the narrowest scope.
principles.rationale: Static checks and executable tests prove different properties and should fail with actionable ownership.
principles.evidence: CI reports each signal independently; a fixture demonstrates each rule can fail; no green static stage is reported as test coverage.

principles.title: Clean deterministic verification
principles.statement: Run release-blocking verification from a clean declared environment and require generated or distributed interfaces to reproduce deterministically.
principles.rationale: Local residue and nondeterministic generation can hide missing inputs or publish output that source does not explain.
principles.evidence: Clean repeated runs pass with frozen dependencies; generated interfaces match committed or packaged output by digest or documented normalization.

principles.title: Risk-based meaningful coverage
principles.statement: Require changed behavior, defect causes, and shared contracts to cover meaningful branches and edge conditions in proportion to risk.
principles.rationale: Line totals can increase while the decisions most likely to harm users remain untested.
principles.evidence: Change review links risks to named assertions; coverage reports show decision and branch gaps; exclusions record a scoped rationale and owner.

principles.title: Positive and negative polarity
principles.statement: Test both accepted and rejected behavior, assert the named-path preconditions, and repeat stateful operations where idempotence or persistence matters.
principles.rationale: A passing happy path does not prove the guard ran, the fixture reached the intended branch, or repetition preserved invariants.
principles.evidence: Paired fixtures prove allow and deny outcomes; preconditions identify the exercised path; repeat tests detect duplicate effects and lost state.

principles.title: Discriminating mutation evidence
principles.statement: Verify important tests can fail by killing a targeted behavior-changing mutation and naming the assertions that discriminate it.
principles.rationale: Executed tests can remain green while never observing the behavior they claim to protect.
principles.evidence: A scoped mutation changes one risk-bearing decision; the expected test fails for the named reason; evidence records assertions rather than fragile aggregate counts.

principles.title: Independent real-world evidence
principles.statement: Derive expected values independently from the recorded result and pin offline real-world observations with revision, date, method, and recheck trigger.
principles.rationale: Self-derived expectations and stale external facts can make tests agree with the same defect or obsolete referent.
principles.evidence: Tests cite an independent oracle or invariant; recorded observations include provenance and expiry conditions; fixtures do not call the implementation to compute their expected result.

principles.title: Executable procedures
principles.statement: Convert every repeatable documented verification procedure into an executable assertion with a known failure mode.
principles.rationale: Manual prose drifts and cannot continuously prove the property it describes.
principles.evidence: Documentation links the executable check; a negative fixture demonstrates failure; unavoidable manual steps name an owner, evidence format, and expiration.

principles.title: Browser trust seam
principles.statement: Treat browser code, rendered input, and client-visible configuration as an untrusted seam.
principles.rationale: Anything delivered to or accepted by a browser can be inspected, modified, or replayed.
principles.evidence: Deployable clients contain no secrets; executable sources are constrained; untrusted content is validated or encoded; browser security tests exercise the seam.

principles.title: Capability-safe enhancement
principles.statement: Detect optional browser capabilities before use and preserve a safe operational baseline when they are absent or fail.
principles.rationale: Browser support, permissions, and runtime resources vary independently of application intent.
principles.evidence: Capability tests disable each optional API; core paths still complete; enhancement failures do not corrupt durable state or block unrelated work.

principles.title: Measured foreground performance
principles.statement: Enforce separate delivery and runtime budgets while prioritizing foreground interaction over background work.
principles.rationale: A small bundle can still run poorly, and background work must not leave active interaction unknown or stuck.
principles.evidence: Per-route size and runtime responsiveness are measured independently; fallible operations have timeouts and progress signals; background work yields under foreground load.

principles.title: Session-safe frontend state
principles.statement: Expose typed frontend states and activate application updates only at a boundary that cannot replace assets beneath a running session.
principles.rationale: Explicit states and atomic activation prevent ambiguous UI behavior and mixed-version execution.
principles.evidence: Contracts enumerate loading, empty, failure, and update states; update tests commit durable state before activation and keep a running session on one asset version.
